Yes,
Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.
distributes medical devices
alongside its massive nationwide pharmaceutical portfolio, though its core device logistics focus historically centers on hospital equipment, diagnostic kits, and consumable supplies rather than consumer-grade wearable tech.
PharmaBoardroom
Overview of Device Distribution
Medical Device Scope:
The company's medical device business covers general hospital equipment, diagnostic reagents, and institutional supply chain services.
Specialized Imports:
They occasionally handle specialized diagnostic or monitoring kits through exclusive or regional import agreements (such as past asthma monitoring or screening tools).
Wearable Focus:
Advanced remote monitoring or consumer wearable health hardware do not form a primary, core highlighted category in their standard commercial catalog.

Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.
is
a major vertically-integrated Chinese pharmaceutical group focused on drug R&D, manufacturing, and nationwide distribution rather than a direct manufacturer of consumer wearables, continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), or remote patient monitoring hardware
Forbes
Core Business Focus
Operates an extensive supply chain and distribution network across China serving tens of thousands of medical institutions.
SPHBIO
Focuses primarily on pharmaceuticals, therapeutic drugs, and retail pharmacy networks rather than proprietary consumer electronics or smart health tracking devices.
SPHBIO
Handles logistics and distribution support for third-party medical products rather than manufacturing independent continuous glucose monitoring or ECG tech.
Digital Health and Wearables Context
Digital health devices like CGMs, wearable ECGs, and smartwatches are largely produced by specialized medical device or consumer tech companies (such as Abbott, Medtronic, Huawei, or Xiaomi).
Grand View Research
While mainstream consumer smartwatches claim non-invasive glucose or ECG tracking via PPG sensors, regulatory bodies note that these wrist-based features function primarily as trend estimators rather than clinical diagnostic replacements.
